frameworks.name: Book-as-Incentive Funnel
frameworks.definition: A distribution mechanism where high-leverage entrepreneurs (with email lists) donate books in bulk, enabling free distribution to entrepreneurs without capital, while aggregating the audience and monetizing through subsequent sales.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi wrote 17 books over two years (blue book to green book) and used them as incentives: entrepreneurs who donated 200 books ($6,000) received codes to distribute to their audiences, enabling centralized redemption and distribution to other entrepreneurs.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Existing high-leverage creator with email list
bounded_by: Requires existing audience with purchasing power
Requires aligned values around giving back

claims.text: Hormozi deliberately built a deeper audience of people with money who share his values; when the opportunity to give back arose, his audience immediately participated at scale.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Creator with 2+ year track record of content delivery
claims.mechanism: Value alignment creates trust and enthusiasm for coordinated action; audience members felt invited to participate in a cause larger than themselves.
bounded_by: Does not apply to audiences built purely on entertainment
Does not apply to creators without demonstrated delivery track record

claims.text: The core win Hormozi prioritized was not the $100 million revenue target, but the outcome of millions of entrepreneurs receiving physical books that are also available free as content and courses.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Creator with capital to absorb product costs

anchors.value: millions and millions of people get books

bounded_by: Only applicable when revenue outcome aligns with giving outcome (coincidence here)

claims.text: Hormozi's book content is deliberately made free across multiple channels (podcast, website, accompanying course) with no opt-in requirement, treating the physical book as a gift/status signal rather than a gating mechanism.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Creator with high gross margins on other products
bounded_by: Does not apply to creators dependent on content monetization (ads, subscriptions)
Does not apply to new creators without audience

examples.text: Hormozi wrote 17 books over two years and created a funnel where entrepreneurs with email lists could donate 200 copies ($6,000) to receive distribution codes. They gave the codes to their audiences, the audiences requested the books, Hormozi redeemed and shipped centrally. This simultaneously distributed millions of free books and generated $106 million in 72 hours through aligned incentives with creators who wanted to give back.

practices.text: Make your primary content free across all platforms (podcast, website, courses with no opt-in) to reduce friction and build deep audience trust.
Use physical books as gifts and status signals rather than paywalled gating mechanisms; treat the book launch as an opportunity to deepen audience alignment around shared values.
